acceptance: UserChangeRequestV1 and IntentInterpretationV1 have closed deterministic schemas, stable identities, exact base/request binding, bounded text/metadata, and fail closed on malformed, stale, mismatched, or out-of-range input.

A valid interpretation is translated without semantic widening into the existing ChangeIntentV1 operation vocabulary; compileUserRequestInterpretation delegates to compileChangeIntent and returns the same deterministic proposed graph delta semantics without accepting it as canonical truth.
Confidence, uncertainty, and provenance remain inspectable proposal metadata only: they cannot grant capability, bypass domain validation, suppress validation issues, or trigger an external effect.

Focused tests cover deterministic identity, request/base mismatch, malformed provenance/uncertainty/confidence, operation forwarding, domain-validation propagation, and no mutation of the request, interpretation, or base graph.

The exact candidate passes full repository format/lint/typecheck/tests, Diffcipline R2, Alibaba OCR deterministic/delegated review where applicable, Jev where available, exact-head CI, and post-merge fresh-main CI before closure.

required: Focused request/interpretation identity-binding and deterministic bridge tests plus full repository gates.
Diffcipline exact-candidate proof, Alibaba OCR accounting/delegated review where applicable, Jev where available, exact-head CI, and post-merge fresh-main CI.

minimality.rationale: The existing ChangeIntentV1 and compileChangeIntent implementation already owns graph-operation semantics and proposal construction. The smallest missing layer is a typed request/interpretation boundary and adapter; duplicating a parser, router, or proposal engine would violate phase ownership.

requirements: Raw user text and interpretation metadata are untrusted proposal input and never grant capability, authorization, trust, or execution authority.
An interpretation must be cryptographically/deterministically identity-bound to the exact request and Product Graph base revision; stale or mismatched interpretations fail closed.
The bridge must preserve existing Change Intent/domain validation and cannot silently drop uncertainty, validation issues, or unsupported operations.

outcome: A raw user change request plus one typed provider-neutral interpretation can be validated, identity-bound, and deterministically compiled through the existing Change Intent compiler into a proposed Product Graph delta while preserving confidence, uncertainty, and provenance and performing no source mutation or provider call.
rationale: SG-000027 and SG-000028 complete deterministic Change Intent proposal semantics but intentionally begin from already-typed ChangeIntent input. The canonical P02-S03 outcome begins from a user request. This final bounded slice adds only the provider-neutral request/interpretation contract and deterministic bridge; model/provider routing remains P03 authority.

risk.recovery: Revert the request-intent boundary module, exports, tests, and evidence. SG-000027 and SG-000028 deterministic Change Intent behavior remains intact and IN-P02-S04 stays blocked.

scope_in: Define a closed UserChangeRequestV1 contract with exact Product Graph base revision, bounded raw user text, deterministic request identity, and explicit request provenance metadata.

Define a closed IntentInterpretationV1 contract bound to the exact request identity and base revision, carrying a bounded ordered ChangeIntent operation set plus explicit confidence, uncertainty notes, and interpretation provenance.

Implement deterministic validation and a bridge that converts a valid request/interpretation pair into the existing ChangeIntentV1 contract and delegates proposal construction to compileChangeIntent without mutating canonical graph state.

Add focused positive/negative tests for request identity binding, base-revision binding, confidence bounds, uncertainty/provenance validation, operation forwarding, deterministic proposal identity, and rejection of stale/mismatched interpretations.
Export the request/interpretation contracts and bridge through the existing @ineractive/product-graph public surface without adding a runtime dependency.
scope_out: No LLM/model/provider invocation, provider routing, prompt construction, tool execution, retrieval, CLM/Jev decision routing, or model-generated interpretation implementation; those remain P03 concerns.
No Question Gate or Assumption Ledger policy; P02-S04 remains the consumer of interpretation confidence/uncertainty once this parent S03 handle closes.
No source mutation, Git mutation, database write, network access, credential use, capability grant, deployment, external effect, UI, or backend compiler behavior.
No new graph-operation semantics beyond SG-000028 and no semantic-reference relation work from P02-S06.
title: IN-P02-S03-T01C user-request intent interpretation boundary
